subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB425.md LANDED - GR3 rides the SAME one substitution as GR2 (MoveClassifier.Sender): a BoundStringLiteral of length zero whose category is Boolean becomes BoundFigurative 'Z', for every receiving operand other than a dynamic-length elementary item. BoundStringLiteral is the one node for the alphanumeric, national and boolean literal forms, so GR2 and GR3 are one two-armed answer keyed on the literal's own category rather than two screens. MEASURED AFTER, against Table 16's Boolean sending row (the only receivers the rule can reach): MOVE B"" TO PIC X(3) stores "000" (Table 17 gives ZERO against an alphanumeric receiving operand the category alphanumeric and 8.3.3.6.4 GR4 gives it the character '0'), into PIC XX/XX it stores "00/00" - the fill is sized by 8.3.3.6.4 GR2 and then EDITED by 14.9.25.4 GR6, so the insertion position keeps its own character - into PIC 1(4) "0000" and into PIC N(3) "000". Golden conformance:2002/pb425_zero_length_literal_move computes all four from the rule. THE SCREENS STILL SEE THE BOOLEAN LITERAL: conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb425-boolean-zero-length-to-numeric pins MOVE B"" TO PIC 9(3) as COBOL0819 at 2002/2014/2023 on Table 16's Boolean-into-Numeric 'No' cell, which is exactly the refusal that would evaporate if the substitution were fed to the syntax rules. DETERMINATION D-B1 (CONFORMANCE.md 3) was required by the neighbouring cell and is recorded rather than guessed: GR2 substitutes figurative SPACE into a BOOLEAN receiver (MOVE "" TO PIC 1(4) is legal - Table 16 admits an alphanumeric sender there and SR7's prohibition names figurative constants written in the source), Table 17 gives SPACE category boolean there, and 8.3.3.6.4 GR5 defines no boolean space; the boolean character '0' is taken, because 14.6.8.6 fills a boolean receiver 'with zero fill or truncation to the right' and 8.3.3.6.4 GR4 is the only boolean character value the standard attaches to a figurative fill - the same answer GR3 gives, so the two arms agree. It is written once, in FigurativeConstants.FillChar, the compiler's one fill-character computation. GR3's OWN exclusion clause stays VACUOUS in the standard and in this compiler alike - 13.18.19.3 SR1 restricts a DYNAMIC LENGTH item's PICTURE to one N or one X, so no boolean dynamic-length item exists to exercise it - recorded so the exclusion is not later mistaken for untested coverage. FINISHER (kb/Work PB425, wave 39): GR1's antecedent is CONDITIONAL - 'If identifier-1 IS a zero-length item' - and 8.5.4's enumeration makes the two sending shapes whose length is not a stable field read conditional in turn, so MoveClassifier.CanBeZeroLengthItem now gates the freeze. 8.5.4 item 9 is a reference-modified data item 'when that has been permitted by use of the compiler directive REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH' (outside such a region 7.3.23.3 GR1 raises EC-BOUND-REF-MOD, so GR1's antecedent can never hold), and 8.5.4 item 6 is 'an intrinsic function that returns a zero-length value' - never a NUMERIC one, whose returned value 15.4 puts in a temporary elementary data item with at least one digit position. Freezing on the SHAPE alone was a wrong answer, not a wasted temp: a numeric function sender was hoisted into SendingValueTemp.FunctionValuePic (21 integer + 9 fraction digits), narrower than a STANDARD-DECIMAL or float result, so MOVE FUNCTION E TO a 31-digit item stored 2718281828000000000000000000000 for 2718281828459045235360287471352 - eight corpus cases measured RED before and GREEN after (pb65_dec_move_channel, pb60_numvalf_native_channels, pb60_numval_standard_decimal, pb251_numval_native_value_fixed, pb253_prose_float_standard_container x3 editions, l1_numval_family_cap_discriminators). The inherited 8.5.1.10 citations for the zero-length-item ENUMERATION were re-derived and repaired to 8.5.4 in the same change set (8.5.1.10 is Dynamic-length elementary items and does not contain the words 'zero-length item'). retired-witness: conformance:2002/pb425_zero_length_literal_move (the golden moved to the 2014 corpus: it writes a zero-length literal, a COBOL-2014 introduction gated by kb/Work PB895 (same program, same expected output))
